summary: Unregister/uninstall cuts the routing block from a user-owned context file (e.g. AGENTS.md) with an awk range that starts at the first begin marker and stops only at an end marker. If the begin marker exists without a following end marker (user deleted the end line, or a stray begin marker), everything from that marker to EOF is deleted; insertBlock (lib/harness-register.ts:378) appends a fresh block in that case, so a later cut removes all user text between the orphan begin and the appended block. Edited skill files get a backup, but this content loss in the user's own file has no backup.

summary: Upgrades and plain setup undo a user's registration choices. `gstack-harness register openclaw --skills all` (or `--skills-dir <dir>`) publishes an installs.tsv row, so `./setup --refresh-registered` (what /gstack-upgrade runs) reruns the child `setup --host openclaw`. That child calls `register openclaw` with no --skills and no --skills-dir. It rewrites the default-dest ledger to router mode and deletes every per-skill folder, or it creates a second, unrequested registration in the default folder. The later `gstack-harness refresh` then reads the rewritten ledger. Plain ./setup inside OpenClaw does the same through `auto` (bin/gstack-harness:123), which registers with defaults and makes refresh skip that id.
fix: Drive both the setup arm and auto from the existing ledger: reuse its mode and dest when a registration exists, and use defaults only for a first install. Or leave harness rows out of the child-setup refresh loop and let `gstack-harness refresh` own them. Add a test: register --skills all, run --refresh-registered, assert mode all.

summary: register() changes the harness folder (removals, backups, writes) before it writes the ledger. Any failure in the loop at line 442 leaves files gstack wrote out of the ledger: ENOSPC, EACCES, a SIGINT, or EXDEV from backupFile's fs.renameSync (line 368) when the state root and the harness folder are on different filesystems, as with a mounted OpenClaw or Dot volume (the bash reader uses mv, which works across filesystems). Every later register then refuses with HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY ('gstack did not write it'), and gstack-uninstall cannot remove those files. EXDEV also surfaces as a raw stack trace, not a HarnessError line.
fix: Write or merge the ledger entries (planned files and created dirs) before mutating, or after each file. Use copy+unlink when rename fails with EXDEV in backupFile.

label: FIXABLE
summary: Cutting the context block can truncate or delete the user's context file. bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:27 uses an awk filter that sets skip=1 on any line containing the begin marker (index(), so the marker counts anywhere in a line) and clears it only on an end marker. When the end marker is missing, everything from the begin marker to the end of the file is dropped. Line 28 then deletes the whole file if what remains is only whitespace. lib/harness-register.ts:375 (insertBlock) makes this layout likely: when it finds a begin marker with no end marker after it, it appends a fresh block at the end of the file instead of repairing the orphan. One deleted end line (from a user, an editor or a merge) therefore leaves an orphan begin marker, a stretch of user content, and then a complete block. The next unregister or uninstall deletes all of that user content. The context file is typically the user's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. Line 28's mv "$tmp" "$file" also resets the file's mode to the umask default. Fix: only cut when a whole-line begin marker is followed by a whole-line end marker. Buffer the lines after a begin marker and print them back if no end marker arrives. insertBlock should refuse an orphan marker, or replace it, rather than append a second block. Preserve the file mode, for example with cat "$tmp" > "$file".

summary: An upgrade silently switches a user's --skills all registration back to router mode. lib/harness-register.ts:396 sets "const mode = opts.mode ?? t.defaultMode" and ignores prev.meta.mode. "gstack-harness register openclaw --skills all" publishes an installs.tsv row, because registry defaults to true and shellRegistry upserts it for render==='host' targets. /gstack-upgrade then runs "setup --refresh-registered", which spawns "setup --host openclaw". That run calls "gstack-harness register openclaw --json --no-registry" without --skills, so OpenClaw gets the default router mode. Every natively listed skill whose bytes are unchanged is deleted, and the run reports status "updated". The parent's later "gstack-harness refresh" (setup:520) then reads the new router mode from the ledger, so the change sticks. Fix: when --skills is absent and a ledger exists for the same id, reuse prev.meta.mode.

label: FIXABLE
summary: A failed write leaves files that no ledger records, which wedges every later register and survives uninstall. lib/harness-register.ts writes every payload file before it writes the ledger at line 456. If the process dies part-way through (ENOSPC, a kill, or an EACCES on one file, any of which throws out of the loop), files are on disk with no ledger row. On a first install, every retry then fails with HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY ("gstack did not write it"), because ownership is derived only from the previous ledger. On an update that adds a new skill folder, refresh fails the same way on every setup and upgrade pass. gstack-uninstall cannot remove those files either, because they are not in any ledger. Fix: before writing, write the ledger (or a pending ledger) holding the union of the previous and planned files and the directories about to be created. Narrow it to the planned set after the writes succeed.

summary: QM registration can publish a pack pinned to an empty or unpushed ref. lib/harness-qm.ts:65 (checkoutCommit) returns '' when git rev-parse fails, for example on a non-git install or a machine without git. It can also return a local commit that does not exist on https://github.com/garrytan/gstack. registerQm still POSTs {url, ref} to create an org-wide pack and writes the ledger (line 92) before the import. The result is an org pack that QM cannot import, or that resolves to a ref nobody intended, plus a retry loop that reuses it. Fix: require a 40-hex ref and refuse with the printed request otherwise. Optionally verify that the ref is reachable on the upstream repository (git branch -r --contains, or ls-remote) before calling the admin API.

summary: Removing a damaged routing block silently deletes the rest of the user's context file. Location: bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:23–28. The awk filter starts skipping at any line containing the begin marker and never resumes if the end marker has been deleted or edited. It then replaces the original context file with the truncated result, without a backup or an error. For example, a context file containing user rules before the begin marker and additional user rules after a missing end marker loses all those later rules on unregister. Marker substrings in quoted examples also trigger the filter. Require a valid, uniquely paired, whole-line marker block before rewriting; preserve the original when the structure is invalid.

label: Medium
summary: Adding a context file to an unchanged registration bypasses ownership tracking. Location: lib/harness-register.ts:429–461. Register generic with --skills-dir X, then rerun the same registration with --skills-dir X --context Y. The “same” predicate compares only mode, names and payload hashes, so the second run skips writeLedger but still inserts a routing block into Y. The ledger therefore never records Y, and unregister leaves its block pointing at the deleted router. Switching an existing registration to a different context file has the same problem. Include context metadata and block ownership in reconciliation, and explicitly reconcile the previous context when it changes.

label: Medium
summary: Unregister forgets ownership even when file removal or backup fails. Location: bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:36–54. Failed rm, mkdir/mv or context-block operations do not stop the loop or contribute to a failure result. The function unconditionally removes the ledger at the end, and its final successful rm makes the caller report success. A read-only destination directory or failed backup write therefore leaves installed files or routing blocks behind while erasing the information needed to remove them safely; a later register can refuse them as unowned. Accumulate failures, return nonzero, and retain ownership records for entries that were not successfully reconciled.

summary: Remote QM removal sends a recorded pack ID to whichever server is currently in the environment. Location: lib/harness-qm.ts:105–110. The ledger identifies the server in meta.dest, and its registration ID is derived from that server, but removeQmPack uses qmAuth(env).url without comparing it to the ledger. After changing GSTACK_QM_URL to another organization or environment, unregister <old-registration-id> --remote can delete an unrelated pack with the same server-local ID on the new server, then discard the old registration even though its pack still exists. Refuse a URL mismatch before issuing DELETE, and bind the remote request to the recorded destination.

summary: Re-registering never reuses the ledger's saved mode or destination, so a documented `--skills all` or `--skills-dir` registration gets reverted. Two paths cause it. First, setup's openclaw/hermes arm runs `gstack-harness register <host>` with no --skills or --skills-dir. /gstack-upgrade (`setup --refresh-registered`) reaches that arm for every openclaw/hermes installs.tsv row by running a child `setup --host openclaw`. Second, plain `./setup` inside OpenClaw runs `gstack-harness auto`, which calls register() with no mode (bin/gstack-harness:123) and adds the id to `done`, so refresh() skips the ledger entry that holds the real mode. In both paths the id is the same (the dest is the same), mode becomes the default `router`, `same` is false, and the previous per-skill folders are deleted as no longer wanted. So OpenClaw's native skill list shrinks to one router after every upgrade or setup rerun, and the new ledger records router, so the choice is lost for good. A `--skills-dir` registration goes the other way: the child setup writes a second copy at the default <home>/.openclaw/skills and adds a second installs.tsv row.
fix: When a ledger already exists for the target, have setup's harness arm and auto take mode and skillsDir from it (or call refresh for that id). Add a test: register openclaw --skills all, run auto or the setup arm, and assert mode stays all and the files are still there.

summary: register() writes the payload files (line 452) before it writes the ledger (line 456). If a first registration fails partway through (ENOSPC, EACCES, an interrupted setup), it leaves files that no ledger lists. The next register then refuses with HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY ('gstack did not write it', line 419), which is false and tells the user to move gstack's own files by hand. gstack-uninstall and unregister also never remove them, because both work only from the ledger.
fix: Before writing any files, write a pending ledger that lists the planned files and dirs (the union with the previous ledger), then rewrite it with the final shas, so ownership and uninstall cover a partial write.

The harness path should take an equivalent lock.

summary: F7 [MEDIUM, INVESTIGATE] The Hermes name-collision check covers only gstack's own folder. Location: lib/harness-register.ts register(), the readdirSync(dest) scan. For Hermes, dest is $HERMES_HOME/skills/gstack. hosts/hermes.ts itself says Hermes indexes skills by frontmatter name and the first match wins (#2825). A user's own review, ship or qa skill anywhere else under $HERMES_HOME/skills will silently shadow gstack's skill, or be shadowed by it, with no HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY refusal. Decide whether to scan the whole Hermes skills tree.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: F8 [LOW, INVESTIGATE] setup --refresh-registered can create a second registration. Location: setup, the refresh loop and the harness arm. For an openclaw or hermes row, the refresh child runs 'setup --host <host>' without the row's destination. The harness arm then registers at t.dest(env) for the current environment. If OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR or HERMES_HOME differs from when the user installed, this creates a second registration at the default path. The parent then refreshes the original through 'gstack-harness refresh', so every Hermes or OpenClaw upgrade renders twice.

label: FIXABLE
summary: F9 [LOW, FIXABLE] Writes and deletes can follow symlinks outside the destination. Location: lib/harness-register.ts. - assertSafeDest checks only the final component of dest, and register checks only top-level entries. - Nested folders under an owned top-level entry (for example dest/gstack/skills/<name>) are written with mkdirSync, writeFileSync and renameSync, all of which follow symlinks. Anything able to write to the harness's skills folder (for example a prompt-injected harness agent) can redirect the next setup refresh to write files anywhere the user can. - Deletion of files from a previous ledger (fs.rmSync(p)) never checks that p is under dest. - walkFiles uses statSync, which follows symlinks and has no guard against cycles. This is the same uid, so it is an integrity problem, not privilege escalation. Fix: check each path component with lstat, or use realpath and require the result to stay under dest. Use lstat in walkFiles.

label: FIXABLE
summary: F10 [LOW, FIXABLE] The QM pack can pin a commit that does not exist upstream. Location: lib/harness-qm.ts registerQm. - checkoutCommit returns '' when git fails, and the request is still sent with ref ''. - The ref is the local HEAD. It can be unpushed, on a fork, or have uncommitted changes, while the URL is fixed to github.com/garrytan/gstack. The org then gets a pack pinned to a commit that does not exist upstream, or one that differs from the local install. - attempt() also retries 401, 403 and 422 responses, not just transient failures. Fix: refuse an empty ref, confirm the ref is on origin before publishing to an organization, and retry only on timeouts and 5xx responses.

label: FIXABLE
summary: F11 [LOW, FIXABLE] Setup reads JSON with sed, which breaks on some paths. Location: setup harness arm, the sed parse of "dest" and "receipt". The pattern [^"]* fails when the destination contains '"' or '\', which JSON escapes. PLAIN rejects only tabs and newlines, so such paths get through. The registry row then stores a truncated or escaped destination, and gstack_install_registry_remove "$target" "$dest" later fails to match it, leaving a stale row. Fix: have gstack-harness print the destination on its own line, or extract it with bun.

label: FIXABLE
summary: F12 [LOW, FIXABLE] Smaller problems: - insertBlock writes the user's context file in place with writeFileSync, so a crash mid-write truncates it. Fix: write a temp file and rename. - 'gstack-harness manifest' never removes its mkdtemp folder, so each call leaves a full host render in /tmp. - unregister() reports a failure of the bash script as HARNESS_NOT_REGISTERED, which sends users to the wrong troubleshooting entry. - 'register <target> --print' prints the generic payload whatever the target is. - In setup, the harness auto block sits after the '_HOOK_REFUSED' exit 1, so harness refresh is skipped whenever hooks are refused. - 'setup --host openclaw --local' silently installs globally. - ancestorIs uses /.(mjs|js|py)$/ with an unescaped dot.

label: INVESTIGATE
summary: F13 [LOW, INVESTIGATE] Detection is loose, and 'status' runs third-party CLIs as a side effect. Location: lib/harness-register.ts TARGETS.present and harnessSees. - Hermes counts as present when any 'hermes' is on PATH, but React Native's Hermes JS engine CLI has the same name. - 'status' runs 'hermes skills list', 'grok inspect' and 'muse skills list' by default, with a 120 s timeout each. Decide whether --no-check should be the default.

label: High
summary: 1. **High — Default uninstall permanently deletes the user edits it claims to preserve.** `bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:35-42`, called by the new block in `bin/gstack-uninstall:268-273`, moves modified registered files into `$GSTACK_STATE_ROOT/backups/harness/`. With the default state root, that is `<home>/.gstack/backups/harness/`. The same uninstall then recursively deletes `<home>/.gstack` at lines 492-495 unless `--keep-state` was supplied. Editing an installed harness skill and running ordinary uninstall therefore deletes both the edited original and its only backup, even though the command prints “kept your edit.” Preserve these backups outside the state tree being removed, or retain that tree when edits were recovered.

label: High
summary: 2. **High — Nested symlinks bypass the registration boundary and let refresh or uninstall modify unrelated files.** `lib/harness-register.ts:403-419,436-453` validates the destination and its immediate skill directories, but never checks intermediate directories below those skill directories. After an OpenClaw router registration, replacing `skills/gstack/skills/gstack-review/sections` with a symlink to another directory passes those checks. Refresh follows that link when hashing, backing up and writing its section files, moving or replacing files outside the registered destination. The uninstall reader has the same problem at `bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:39-42`: `[ ! -L "$b" ]` checks only the final file, so it deletes matching external files or moves differing external files through a symlinked ancestor. An agent able to alter its harness folder can redirect a later installer/uninstaller into unrelated user data or the checkout. Validate every path component and containment immediately before destructive operations; checking only the top-level directory is insufficient.

label: Medium
summary: 3. **Medium — A missing context end marker causes uninstall to erase the remainder of the user's rules file.** `bin/gstack-harness-ledger.sh:23-28` sets `skip=1` on a begin marker and writes the filtered output back without first requiring a corresponding end marker. If a person accidentally removes or changes the generated end marker, every subsequent user-authored line is discarded. Feeding the exact awk expression a rules header, a begin marker, routing text and a trailing user rule produces only the header. `insertBlock` at `lib/harness-register.ts:375-381` also appends a fresh block after an unmatched old begin marker, so re-registering before uninstall does not repair the damage: removal spans the old begin through the newly appended end. Refuse malformed or ambiguous marker pairs without rewriting the file.

label: Medium
summary: 4. **Medium — Changing the context file can leave routing behind and remove the wrong block on uninstall.** `lib/harness-register.ts:399-401,429-461` derives the registration ID from `--skills-dir` when present, and its `same` comparison ignores context metadata. Register generic with a skills directory and context file A, then rerun with the same skills directory and context file B. The payload is unchanged, so the ledger is not rewritten, but `insertBlock` still writes B. The ledger continues to record only A; unregister removes A's block and the router while leaving B's now-broken routing instructions behind. Removing `--context` similarly leaves the old block tracked and installed. Include context identity in reconciliation and explicitly remove the previous owned block when its destination changes.

label: Medium
summary: 5. **Medium — Repeated router/all mode changes become permanently blocked by gstack's own empty directories.** `lib/harness-register.ts:412-419,435-459` determines ownership exclusively from the previous ledger's files. When switching from `all` to `router`, it removes obsolete files but leaves their directories in place; those directories survive only in `prev.dirs`. Switching back to `all` then finds those existing skill directories, sees no corresponding file ownership in the router ledger, and throws `HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY`. For example, OpenClaw `router -> all -> router -> all` fails on the last registration even without user changes. Prune obsolete empty directories during the transition or recognize safely recorded directory ownership instead of treating the installer's own leftovers as foreign entries.

label: Medium
summary: 6. **Medium — Remote QM removal is not bound to the server recorded in the registration.** `lib/harness-qm.ts:105-110` reads the pack ID from the selected ledger but builds authentication and the DELETE destination solely from the current environment. It never compares `auth.url` with `l.meta.dest`. After changing `GSTACK_QM_URL` from one QM instance to another, `unregister <old-registration-id> --remote` sends the old instance's pack ID to the new instance. This at least makes the recorded registration impossible to remove with the selected environment; if instances share IDs through a database clone, it archives the wrong organization's pack. Reject a URL mismatch before sending a request and require credentials for the recorded origin.

label: Medium
summary: 7. **Medium — An interrupted first registration leaves files that neither retry nor uninstall can manage.** `lib/harness-register.ts:442-459` writes the actual destination files before persisting any ownership ledger, with no rollback or recovery journal. A disk-full error, permission failure on a later file, or process termination after the first successful write leaves a partial install with no ledger. Retrying then rejects the already-created top-level directory at lines 415-419 as `HARNESS_UNOWNED_ENTRY`; uninstall cannot discover it because it reads only ledgers. This also affects automatic registration during setup, turning a transient failure into a manual-repair requirement. Persist recoverable ownership before publishing files, or stage and roll back a failed installation without leaving untracked destination entries.
